consensus_summary: Nineveh conventionally signifies a wicked Gentile city whose people repent, receive divine mercy, and stand as witnesses against the unrepentant; it also has a complementary judgment-on-empire motif.
book_summary: Nineveh signifies repentant Gentile peoples who rise in judgment against the unrepentant, described as a great city of the sea.
consensus_core_identification: Repentant Gentiles who exemplify repentance and condemn unrepentant hearers.
book_core_identification: Gentile peoples who repent and rise in judgment.
boundary_disagreement: No material boundary disagreement. The book selects the standard Matthew/Jonah repentance motif without discussing Nineveh's additional role as an oppressive empire under judgment; omission of that complementary motif does not amount to its rejection.
rationale: The book's core identification closely matches the consensus's primary Jonah–Matthew reading: Nineveh represents repentant Gentiles whose response condemns the unrepentant. The phrase “great city of the sea” adds imagery but does not replace or materially alter that central referent.
strongest_objection: Matthew 12:41 directly supports repentance and rising in judgment, but the printed citation alone does not establish “city of the sea” and only indirectly supports extending the historical men of Nineveh into a general symbol of Gentile peoples.
